name: France
summary: France is easier for vegans than its butter-and-cheese reputation suggests. Bakery bread, Provençal vegetable dishes and Nice's chickpea socca are vegan by tradition, and Paris has a large fully vegan restaurant scene. Outside cities, expect to ask for dishes without butter, cream or lardons.
phrase: Je suis végane. Je ne mange ni viande, ni poisson, ni œufs, ni produits laitiers, ni beurre, ni miel.

regions.text: The easiest part of France. The cooking is built on olive oil, vegetables and chickpeas: socca and pissaladière in Nice, panisse in Marseille, ratatouille and tian everywhere.
Has more vegan restaurants than anywhere else in France, plus Lebanese, North African, Vietnamese and Indian food. Classic bistros are harder, but most will make a vegetable plate.
Butter and cream country. Buckwheat galettes are your best bet, and crêperies are used to changing fillings.
Heavy on pork, cheese and cream. Tarte flambée has crème fraîche and bacon. Big towns such as Strasbourg and Lille have vegan cafés.
Duck fat is the default cooking fat, including for potatoes. Bordeaux and Toulouse have vegan options; villages are harder.

eating_out: Weekly markets (marchés) are the best place to eat vegan by tradition: bread, olives, fruit, roasted chestnuts and, in the south, socca.
Bakeries: a baguette or country loaf is usually vegan. Croissants and pains au chocolat are made with butter.
In bistros, ask for the seasonal vegetables (légumes de saison) without butter. Side dishes are often the easiest way to build a meal.
Lebanese and North African restaurants are reliable. Ask whether the couscous broth is vegetable or meat.
'Végétarien' on a menu usually means cheese or egg. Look for 'végan', 'végétalien' or '100% végétal'.
shopping: Supermarkets carry plant milks, tofu, hummus and vegan ready meals. Organic chains such as Biocoop have the widest range.
Look for 'végétal', 'végan' or the V-Label on packs.
A picnic from a market and a bakery is one of the best meals in France, and fully vegan.

faqs.q: Is it hard to be vegan in France?
faqs.a: Not in the big cities. Paris, Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux all have vegan restaurants. In rural areas, rely on markets, bakeries and vegetable sides, and ask for no butter.
Usually. French rules for a 'baguette de tradition' allow only flour, water, salt, and yeast or leaven, so no milk, butter or egg.

faqs.q: Are French fries vegan in France?
faqs.a: Usually they are fried in vegetable oil, but some places, especially in the north, use beef fat. Ask: 'Huile végétale ?'
Not always. Many wines are fined with egg white, milk protein or gelatin. Wines labelled 'vin végan' are not.

name: Spain

Papas arrugadas with mojo are vegan and everywhere. Gofio, toasted grain flour, is a local staple.

eating_out: The set lunch (menú del día) usually has a vegetable first course. Ask whether it has ham or meat stock.
In tapas bars, build a meal from several small vegetable plates: pan con tomate, padrón peppers, olives, patatas bravas without aioli, garlic mushrooms.
'Vegetariano' often still means egg or cheese. Say 'vegano' and spell it out: no meat, fish, egg or dairy.
Spaniards eat late: lunch is around 2 to 4 pm and dinner after 9 pm. Kitchens may be closed in between.
Mixed salad (ensalada mixta) almost always comes with tuna and egg.
shopping: Supermarkets stock soy and oat milk, tofu, hummus and vegan burgers, often with 'apto para veganos' on the label.
Food markets (mercados) have excellent fruit, vegetables, olives, nuts and bread for a picnic.

name: the United States

regions.text: Los Angeles, San Francisco, Portland and Seattle are among the easiest cities in the world for vegans, with fully vegan restaurants, bakeries and doughnut shops.

Vegetable side dishes are often cooked with pork or butter, even greens and beans. Atlanta, Austin, Nashville and New Orleans have good vegan restaurants.
Harder outside the cities. Chicago and Minneapolis are easy; elsewhere rely on Mexican, Indian, Thai and chain restaurants with allergen menus.
Tex-Mex and New Mexican food is bean- and chilli-based. Ask whether the beans and tortillas are made with lard.

eating_out: American servers expect requests for changes. Say 'vegan' and spell it out: no meat, dairy, eggs or honey.
Big chain restaurants publish allergen and ingredient menus online, which makes checking quick.
Ethiopian restaurants are excellent for vegans: lentil and vegetable stews on injera. Ask for no spiced butter (niter kibbeh).
Thai, Indian and Mexican restaurants are easy fallbacks. Ask about fish sauce, ghee and lard.
shopping: Whole Foods and Trader Joe's have big vegan ranges. Regular supermarkets stock plant milks, tofu and vegan meat.
US food labels must name major allergens, including milk and egg, often in a bold 'Contains:' line. It's the quickest first check.

regions.text: The easiest part of Italy: olive-oil cooking, vegetables and legumes. Caponata, panelle, granita and pasta with tomato and aubergine.
Fave e cicoria, orecchiette with greens (ask about anchovies), taralli, friselle and some of Italy's best vegetables.
Pizza bianca, artichokes, chicory, beans and aglio e olio. Rome has a good number of vegan restaurants.
Tuscans are called 'bean-eaters' (mangiafagioli). Ribollita, pappa al pomodoro, panzanella and white beans with olive oil.
Butter, cheese, egg pasta and risotto make it harder. Milan, Turin and Bologna have vegan restaurants; in the countryside ask for vegetable sides.

eating_out: Vegetable side dishes (contorni) are your friend: grilled vegetables, greens with garlic, roast potatoes, beans.
Pizzerias will make most pizzas without cheese ('senza formaggio'). The marinara is vegan as standard.
Dried pasta is usually egg-free. Fresh pasta (pasta fresca, pasta all'uovo) and tagliatelle usually contain egg.
Many bars now sell a vegan croissant (cornetto vegano) for breakfast.
If you're staying at a farm stay (agriturismo), tell them in advance and they'll often cook specially.
shopping: Supermarkets stock plant milks (look for 'bevanda di soia' or 'bevanda d'avena'), tofu, and vegan ranges.
Markets are excellent for fruit, vegetables, olives and bread. A bakery (forno) sells pizza by the slice.

The pizza marinara is: tomato, garlic, oregano and olive oil. Most other pizzas can be made without cheese.
Classic pesto genovese contains parmesan and pecorino, so no. Some shops sell vegan pesto.
Milk-based gelato isn't, but fruit sorbets and granita usually are, and many gelaterie mark vegan flavours.

name: India

name: New Zealand
summary: New Zealand is where I'm from, and it's an easy country for vegans. Cafés in every town have plant milk and a vegan option, supermarkets label vegan food, and the produce is superb. Small rural towns are harder, but bakeries and supermarkets fill the gaps.

faqs.q: Is New Zealand good for vegans?
faqs.a: Yes. Cities have plenty of vegan options, cafés everywhere have plant milk, and supermarkets label vegan food clearly.

faqs.q: Can I bring food into New Zealand?
faqs.a: You must declare all food when you arrive, and fresh fruit and vegetables are usually not allowed. Fines apply if you don't declare.

faqs.q: Are New Zealand bakery pies vegan?
faqs.a: Traditional pies have meat and butter pastry, but many bakeries now sell vegan pies. Ask.
